title: A New File Type Silently Changes the Prompt

turns.userMessage: Let's build a new REST endpoint for exporting reports.
turns.assistantResponse: Sure, looking at the API layer.
turns.explanation: Normal first turn — writes the static system prompt/instructions plus this turn's own content. No path-scoped `.instructions.md` files are relevant yet, since no matching file type has been touched.

turns.userMessage: Use the existing pagination helper for the export list.
turns.assistantResponse: Sure, reusing the existing pagination helper.
turns.explanation: Normal turn; reads/extends the cache built by turn 1. Still no `.sql` files touched.

turns.userMessage: Also add a migration for the new export_jobs table.
turns.assistantResponse: Adding the migration — I'll follow the SQL migration conventions.
turns.explanation: This is the first turn to touch a *.sql file — which silently pulls in a path-scoped .instructions.md (applyTo: **/*.sql) that turns 1-2 never triggered. Nothing about the user's message looks like a config change, but because the client groups this block with the other stable instructions near the top of the prompt, inserting it breaks the prefix match at that position — invalidating everything cached after it, all prior conversation included, even though none of that conversation actually changed. The full 4,100-token history must be resent uncached, and a new cache builds from scratch including the newly-included instructions block. Unlike an explicit model switch or MCP tool change, this turn carries no visible trigger tag in the turns table — that's the whole danger: the cache reset looks, from the UI, just like an ordinary turn, yet costs about 5x as much.

turns.userMessage: Add an index on export_jobs.created_at too.
turns.assistantResponse: Adding the index to the migration.
turns.explanation: Normal turn under the newly-included SQL instructions block; the cache rebuilds under the new prefix, same shape as any healthy cache-building turn.

turns.assistantResponse: Sounds good, let me know if you need anything else.
turns.explanation: Cache continues building normally under the new prefix, with no further disruption — but nothing in this session ever visibly flagged that turn 3's spike happened at all.
